I read the famous hard drive lifespan article when it came out for desktop and server hard drives, Without a doubt HST drives were the top performer, but what about mobile hard drives? can anyone recommend a 2tb laptop hard drive with a good track record?

HGST is the most often rated for long-life and reliability. Followed by Western Digital. For WD drives, avoid any Red, Green or Purple drives, if they even make those for 2.5 inch. They're specially designed for non-OS drive purposes. Stick with Black or Blue WD drives.

HGST does make a 1.5TB 2.5, but it's a 5400 RPM.

Avoid any drives in the 5400 RPM category. They will impact the performance of your laptop.

If your laptop is fairly new, it may contain an mSATA slot, as well as a 2.5 slot. If so, get yourself a decent size mSATA SSD and then you can have a much lower impact from using a 5400 RPM as a D-Drive for app installs, data, etc.

Perfect advice thank you. I will be using the drive as a backup storage, and the SSD for my system drive.

I had problems with WD in the past on desktop machines. but I have to admit they were far better than the old barracuda hard drives. I had nothing but constant problems with them.

As for laptop drives, I would by happy to pay out a little extra for a decent drive. I have heard bad things about Samsung drives, but I've read so many conflicting reviews, I thought it was time to ask for someones else opinion.

I already have a 1.5tb external drive, but its the larger 3.5. I;m hoping to condense everything into one unit..

Do you think the HGST 1.5tb 2.5 would be more reliable than the WD Black or Blue?

Just from the performance / reliability review of the 3.5s, I would assume HGST's 2.5 may mirror the same results. Hopefully.

I would never touch a Seagate again. I had a 4-drive Seagate NAS, and of the 4 drives, 6 failed in under three years. All of the original 4, and then two of the replacements. I ditched that shit and went to Synology and used WD Red drives which have been going 24/7 for nearly two years without a single failure.

Outside of the Seagate NAS drives, nearly ever other Seagate drive I've had has failed. I believe I no longer have any as none of them had a long life. I only use WD drives now, but have always considered getting an HGST, but I seem to always catch the WD's on sale for a lower comparative price.

I think the HGST 1.5TB may be hard to get, since it's very new. So likely the option would be a Travelstar 7K1000

For WD, it would be the WD10JPLX

It would be great if they made Red/Purple drives in 2.5 format. I just installed a 8TB Purple in a friends media PC. The great thing about the Purple series - they're meant for 24/7 use in high temp environments, but like Green drives, they cannot be used in hardware RAID setups.

For a NAS, the RED drives are perfect. Enterprise / 24/7 use. Great products.

So for WD, and HGST, their regular 2.5 drives would likely not stand up to 24/7 and heat. But for a laptop that's turned on and off, they're still great.
